scopeRule: Natural gas pipelines tied to the US data center buildout, at ANY length (Baird 2026-10-16, no floor): a transmission line, lateral, loop or expansion whose sourced purpose is to supply a data center, a data center campus, or a gas power plant built for one or tied to data center load by its owner, developer or utility (ruling 6, 2026-10-18). Compression-only expansions tied to data centers count (LengthKnown 0). OUT: pipe inside the plant fence, local utility distribution mains, field gathering, and power-plant laterals with no data center tie (those are monitor when under 25 km; 25 km or more was covered by the 2026-10-02 discovery). Crude, NGL and refined-product lines are out of scope. If you cannot establish a length, still emit it and say 'length unknown'.
vetRule: (d) DATA CENTER RULES (Baird 2026-10-16, docs/plans/2026-10-16_us-gas-datacenter-subfloor.md). 1 (loosened later on 2026-10-16): DataCenter = yes with a validated ref that names THIS pipeline and mentions data centers at all as a demand driver or a reason for the project (the filing, the developer, the shipper, EIA, or press). One of several named drivers counts; so does a shipper whose demand for this project the source ties to data centers. Data center talk that is company-wide and not about this project, comes only from opponents, or concerns another row leaves DataCenter blank with a note in researcher_notes. 2: a compression-only expansion tied to data centers is a new_row with LengthKnown = 0, LengthKnownUnits = mi (or km as the source states), Diameter blank, RouteType 'Capacity expansion only', RouteAccuracy 'no route', in the parent-system / SegmentName shape of (e); the parent row is not tagged for it. 3: no length floor for a pipeline tied to data centers; in-fence plant piping and utility distribution mains are out. A sourced line with no data center tie and under 25 km -> class monitor, monitor_reason 'no data center tie'. (e) EXPANSION ROWS: GEM tracks US expansion projects as their own rows, with PipelineName = the parent system's GEM PipelineName exactly as the roster spells it and SegmentName = the project (e.g. P2544 'Transcontinental Gas Pipeline' / 'Hillabee Expansion Project, Phase 2'). An expansion with no row of its own is a new_row in that shape, not a match to the parent system's row. A project that IS an existing row under another name is matched_existing. (f) EIA (sources/eia_pipeline_projects/NOTES.md): cite the DATED release that states the value as https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/<file> (newest is EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx; never the undated twin), sheet + Excel row in the note, url_verifier with --name set to the EIA project name. Local copies are in sources/eia_pipeline_projects/raw/. Pair EIA with a FERC order/filing, a state regulator document or an operator release when cheap. EIA 'Cost (millions)' -> stage the full number (450 -> 450000000, USD). EIA miles -> LengthKnown in mi, never converted. EIA 'Additional Capacity' is INCREMENTAL MMcf/d for an expansion. Status: Announced/Pre-filing/Applied/Approved -> proposed, Construction -> construction, Completed -> operating, On Hold -> shelved, Cancelled/Denied -> cancelled. Month cells are integers 1-12. (g) Country = United States; Puerto Rico is out of scope. Intrastate lines never appear in FERC: FERC silence is not an existence concern; check the state regulator (Texas RRC T-4 etc.). (h) Owner names in the ownership team's style: run scripts/entity_lookup.py and scripts/entity_style.py, adopt the team's spelling on an exact/alias hit only. Notes are plain language for a person: short sentences, sources named by what they are, no repo jargon, no em-dashes or arrows. (i) RULINGS 6 TO 8 (Baird 2026-10-18), on top of (d). 6: a tie THROUGH A POWER PLANT counts. A pipeline, lateral or expansion that supplies a gas plant is DataCenter = yes when the plant's own filings, its developer, or the utility tie THAT PLANT to data center load. A named campus or customer is high specificity; data center load named among the plant's reasons is medium. Company-wide resource-plan talk about data centers, not about this plant, stays blank. The ref for the tag must name the pipeline; a second ref may carry the plant's data center tie, and DataCenterNotes says how the two connect (pipeline serves plant X; plant X is tied to data center Y by source Z). Tag the expansion or lateral serving the plant, never a legacy mainline it hangs off. 7: big interstate expansions with such an indirect tie are included. 8: ENDPOINTS ARE NOT NEEDED for a data center pipeline row. For a pipeline tied to data centers, the add-threshold is met by (a) an identified sponsor and (b) a named project in a known state (the county when given); a public announcement, filing or permit by the sponsor naming the project is the concrete step. StartLocation, EndLocation, LengthKnown and the route stay blank until a source gives them (RouteAccuracy 'no route'). This loosening applies to data center rows only.

seedIntro:
Seeds come from two sources, named by the seed_id prefix.
recheck: a lead an earlier data center pass left on the monitor list, now marked for re-check because rulings 6 to 8 (2026-10-18) may turn it into a row or a tag: a tie through a power plant now counts, and endpoints are not needed. The hint carries the last researcher's reason and the run it came from. It is a starting point, never a conclusion: re-research the tie under the new rulings, and when the sponsor and project are named, stage the row even without endpoints or length. When the pipeline turns out to be an existing roster row, it is 'matched' (a DataCenter tag lead for that row) with the ref that ties it to data centers in evidence.
survey: a new lead from the 2026-10-18 web survey of gathering, utility and Texas permit infrastructure. The hint carries what the survey found and the URLs it read; verify everything yourself. Several Texas leads come from Texas Railroad Commission new construction reports (Form PS-48 PDFs); a report is a valid ref for the line's operator, county, length, diameter and start date, but a data center tie guessed from a line's NAME is not a tie: find a source that says what the line serves. Check the roster first: some survey leads may already be rows (Hugh Brinson P8318 Abilene Laterals, Licking County Pipeline P8320, Prosperity Line P8234, Transwestern Green Chile P8290).
Outcome codes for the ledger reason (start with one): NEW_ROW, EXISTING_ROW (matched, tag lead), ONSITE_NO_PIPE, NOT_FOUND, NO_DC_TIE (pipeline real, no data center tie even under ruling 6), OUT_OF_SCOPE.
seedSearch: COMPREHENSIVE SEARCH, focused on the two questions the new rulings open: (A) is there a source tying this pipeline, or the power plant it feeds, to data center load (the plant's air permit or siting case, the utility's certificate or rate case for THIS plant, the developer's or hyperscaler's release, the large-load or electric service agreement docket); (B) who sponsors the pipeline and what is it called (FERC eLibrary and Federal Register for CP dockets and blanket prior notices, the state regulator or siting board, the Texas Railroad Commission new construction reports and T-4 permits, midstream earnings releases and call transcripts, trade press). Search with several name variants (project, plant, campus, developer, county). A blocked page is not a dead end: run python scripts/fetch.py <url> --head 4000, then the Wayback copy. For EIA seeds, cite the dated release URL https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/<file>. GOGPT and gem.wiki stay leads only, never refs.
seedBudget: Budget: at least 6 distinct web searches per seed, more when a lead appears; read the most promising pages in full (python scripts/fetch.py <url>). Pace searches a few seconds apart; if a search fails, wait and retry before giving up. End each ledger reason with 'Searches run: N.' and a plain list of the sources checked and what each showed.
extra:
## This run: United States gas DATA CENTER re-vet, 2026-10-19, seeds only, national.
38 seeds: leads an earlier pass left on the monitor list that the 2026-10-18 rulings may turn into rows or tags, and new leads from the 2026-10-18 infrastructure survey. Rulings 6 to 8 (in the vet rule): a tie through a power plant counts, big interstate expansions with an indirect tie are in, and a data center pipeline needs only a sponsor and a named project, not endpoints.
Read the priorStaging runs only to learn which new rows and matches they already staged, so you never stage the same line twice. A seed they left monitor or dropped is re-researched in full.
The roster below is the FULL national roster (pulled 2026-10-19, including the rows appended 2026-10-16 and 10-17): match against all of it. A matched_existing / EXISTING_ROW finding is a DataCenter tag lead for that row: put the ref that ties the row to a data center in its evidence. Do not suggest a plant or campus name as an OtherEnglishNames.
GOGPT (GEM plant tracker) and gem.wiki are leads only, never refs. Crude, NGL and refined-product lines are out of scope. Puerto Rico and everything outside the US are out of scope.
